name: Calculate and approve pool unit prices
summary: Each business day the custodian calculates a net asset value and unit value for every pool, and the model manager's four-person unit pricing team checks it before it is used to issue and redeem client units. An analyst confirms the NAV pack is complete, that positions are reconciled, works through price exceptions and stale prices, checks accruals and units outstanding, compares the day's return with the benchmark and proposes the price; the manager approves it. Most elapsed time is the custodian's overnight run and the morning wait for reconciliations; most rework comes from price challenges and custodian re-runs. A price later found wrong must be quantified against the NAV error policy and, if material, every affected client transaction reprocessed.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about 240 staff running four to five unitised pools for a handful of public pension and insurance clients, with a global custodian calculating NAVs.
baseline.notes: Pools are daily priced; one pool (public market alternatives) holds hedge funds valued monthly and from 2022 the infrastructure pool holds private assets valued quarterly. 2021 state with four pools is the base.

unit_of_work: one pool unit price for one valuation date
trigger: The valuation point (4 p.m. Eastern) passes on a business day and the custodian runs its overnight NAV calculation for the pool.
end_state: The manager has approved the unit value, it is confirmed to the custodian and loaded in the unitholder register and downstream systems; or, for a price found wrong later, the error is corrected and the incident closed.

volume.seasonality: Flat across the year; one price per pool per business day. Volume steps up as pools launch (one pool late 2020, four in 2021, five in 2022). Month and quarter ends add hedge fund and private asset value updates and heavier accrual checks.

evidence.note: Organisation file process map and pools-in-operation driver (4 pools x 21 business days); daily dealing of public market pools at a peer is described by BCI.

roles.title: Analyst, pool unit pricing and transfer agency
roles.department: Pool unit pricing and transfer agency

evidence.note: Three analysts also run unit transactions; about 1.45 FTE on daily pricing for four pools is an author estimate. Cost from the organisation file.

roles.title: Manager, pool unit pricing and transfer agency
roles.department: Pool unit pricing and transfer agency

evidence.note: Daily approval of four prices plus incidents; FTE is an author estimate. Cost from the organisation file.
Price challenge research on about four in ten pool prices; author estimate.
Occasional accrual rate confirmations; author estimate.
Daily check of the alternatives pool's non-daily-priced holdings; author estimate.
Approves material error corrections a few times a year; author estimate.

systems.name: Custodian portal (custody, accounting records, net asset value reports, cash and corporate action notices)
Market data terminals and vendor feeds (prices, indices, reference data)
Pool unitholder register and transfer agency records (custodian module with controlled spreadsheets)
Order management, pre-trade compliance and investment book of record platform (vendor software as a service)
Private markets investment accounting and monitoring system (commitments, calls, distributions, valuations)
Investment data warehouse and business intelligence reports
Corporate ERP (general ledger, accounts payable, budgeting)
Email, video calls and collaboration suite

steps.name: Lock the valuation point and open the pricing cycle
steps.description: At the 4 p.m. Eastern valuation point the custodian's fund accounting platform closes the pool's trade capture for the valuation date and captures closing prices, exchange rates and that day's unit transactions. Nothing is touched by the model manager staff; the step only opens the cycle and decides whether the next business day follows tonight or after a weekend or holiday.
inputs: trades and unit transactions for the valuation date

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: next day is a business day
valuation date falls before a weekend or holiday

evidence.note: About 52 Fridays and 8 to 9 weekday holidays out of about 251 valuation days lead into a non-business day; calendar count by the author.

steps.name: Hold the cycle over the weekend or holiday
steps.description: When the valuation date is a Friday or the day before a holiday, the custodian produces the NAV pack on the next business day and the model manager's unit pricing team reviews it that morning. The price waits through the non-business days with no work done.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Two days for a weekend, three for a long weekend; author estimate.

steps.name: Custodian prices holdings and strikes the draft NAV
steps.description: Overnight the custodian loads vendor prices for every listed security, translates foreign holdings at the closing exchange rates, books income and expense accruals and the day's subscriptions and redemptions, and calculates a draft net asset value and unit value for each pool. It runs its own price tolerance and stale price checks under controls that its CSAE 3416 (SOC 1) report describes.

error.defect_description: A wrong vendor price, a missed corporate action or a mis-booked accrual enters the draft NAV.

control.basis: Custodian's CSAE 3416 / SOC 1 Type 2 report covering NAV calculation and pricing controls

evidence.note: Custodian-calculated daily NAV for pools is described by the sources; the overnight run ending between 4 a.m. and 11 a.m. is an author estimate.

steps.name: Publish NAV pack and exception reports to the portal
steps.description: The custodian portal publishes the draft NAV pack for each pool: holdings and prices, the trial balance, income and expense accruals, units outstanding, the unit value and the custodian's price exception, stale price and large movement reports. A scheduled job copies the files to the model manager's shared pricing folder.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Typical custodian reporting; publishing delay is an author estimate.

steps.name: Check the NAV pack is complete
steps.description: The unit pricing analyst opens the pack for the pool and confirms that every report is present and dated for the right valuation date, that the number of holdings and accounts matches yesterday's pack plus known changes, and that the pool's sub-accounts for each external manager are all included.

error.defect_description: A missing sub-account or wrong-dated report is not noticed.

next.condition: report missing, late or for the wrong date

evidence.note: Pre-close readiness checks are described by the source; times and the 7% incomplete share are author estimates.

steps.name: Chase the custodian for missing or late reports
steps.description: The analyst emails and phones the custodian's fund accounting client service team, names the missing report or sub-account, and asks for a re-run or re-issue with an expected time. The manager is copied when the delay threatens the dealing cut-off for that day's unit transactions.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Common practice with outsourced fund accounting; author estimate.

steps.name: Custodian re-issues the NAV pack
steps.description: The custodian's team finds the missing feed or sub-account, re-runs the NAV for the pool and republishes the pack to the portal. The pricing team waits; other pools carry on in parallel.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate of custodian turnaround.

steps.name: Confirm positions and cash are released by reconciliations
steps.description: The analyst checks the reconciliations team's release note or dashboard for the pool's custody and manager accounts and reads any open position or cash break larger than the pricing materiality limit. A clean release means the custodian's holdings behind the NAV agree with the model manager's book of record.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Unit pricing procedure: holdings and cash reconciled in each pricing cycle before the price is approved (good practice in ASIC/APRA RG 94)

next.condition: no open break above the limit
material break open on a pool account

evidence.note: Sources describe reconciliation in each pricing cycle and stop-the-line on unreconciled positions; the 10% share and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Resolve an open break with the reconciliations team
steps.description: The analyst asks the reconciliation analyst which side is right, for example an unsettled trade or a corporate action the custodian has booked but the model manager has not, and agrees whether the NAV needs an adjustment or the break is a timing item that does not affect the price. The outcome is noted on the pricing checklist.

error.defect_description: A timing break that does affect the NAV is waved through.

evidence.note: Author estimate; depends on the reconciliations team's queue that morning.

steps.name: Review price exceptions, stale prices and exchange rates
steps.description: The analyst works through the custodian's exception reports for the pool: securities whose price moved more than the tolerance for their asset type, prices unchanged for several days, missing or zero prices, differences between primary and secondary vendors, and the exchange rates used. Each item is either explained, for example by company news or a market move, or marked for challenge.

error.defect_description: A wrong price within the tolerance band passes unnoticed.

control.basis: Pool valuation policy and unit pricing procedure: price tolerance, stale price and secondary source checks (RG 94 good practice)

next.condition: one or more prices to challenge

evidence.note: Tolerance, stale, zero-price and FX checks are described by RG 94; the 38% challenge rate for pools holding thousands of global and emerging market securities is an author estimate.

steps.name: Research questioned prices with investment data management
steps.description: An investment data analyst looks up the questioned securities on market data terminals and the alternative vendor, checks for halts, corporate actions or delistings, and agrees an override price or confirms the original. The agreed price and its source are recorded in the price challenge log and sent to the custodian.

error.defect_description: An override price is keyed with a wrong decimal or for the wrong share class.

evidence.note: Security pricing support from the data team is common practice; author estimate.

steps.name: Custodian applies price overrides and re-runs the NAV
steps.description: The custodian keys the agreed override prices, re-runs the pool NAV and republishes the revised pack. The analyst waits for the new unit value before moving on to accruals.

error.defect_description: Override keyed incorrectly by the custodian.

evidence.note: NAV reruns are a recognised breakpoint (FundCount) but the turnaround is an author estimate.

steps.name: Check income and corporate action accruals
steps.description: The analyst compares dividend and interest accruals in the trial balance with the day's ex-dates and coupon schedule, checks withholding tax rates on foreign dividends, and confirms that splits, mergers and spin-offs effective today are reflected in both quantities and prices.

error.defect_description: A missed dividend accrual or wrong withholding rate is not caught.

evidence.note: Accrual review is part of the described NAV workflow; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Check cost recovery and manager fee accruals
steps.description: The analyst checks that the daily accrual for the model manager's cost recovery charge and for each external manager's fee uses the rates in the current accrual schedule from investment accounting and that the running month-to-date totals look right against the pool's size.

error.defect_description: An outdated fee rate stays in the accrual.

evidence.note: Expenses recovered through the unit value and incorrect fee rates as an error source are described; frequency is an author estimate.

steps.name: Investment accounting confirms an accrual rate
steps.description: A senior investment accountant confirms the new cost recovery allocation rate or a changed external manager fee schedule, sends the updated accrual schedule, and asks the custodian to adjust the accrual if it was wrong.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Rate changes cluster at month and quarter starts and manager hires; author estimate.

steps.name: Agree units outstanding to the unitholder register
steps.description: The analyst compares the units outstanding in the NAV pack with the closing units in the unitholder register after the valuation date's subscriptions, redemptions and switches, client by client, and investigates any difference before the unit value is used.

error.defect_description: A unit transaction booked on the wrong date leaves units out of agreement but within rounding.

control.basis: Units in issue agreed to the register each valuation date; tested by the external auditor and in the custodian's CSAE 3416 report

next.condition: pool holds hedge funds or private assets valued less often

evidence.note: Reconciling units and recording unit transactions on a trade date basis are described; the 25% share reflects one of four pools (public market alternatives) and later the infrastructure pool.

steps.name: Valuations confirms values of non-daily-priced holdings
steps.description: For the public market alternatives pool, and from 2022 the infrastructure pool, a senior valuation analyst checks that each hedge fund or private holding is carried at the latest administrator estimate or valuation committee value, rolled forward for cash flows since, and flags any new monthly fund NAV that has arrived.

error.defect_description: A stale hedge fund value stays in the pool after a newer estimate arrived.

control.basis: Pool valuation policy: fair value of non-daily-priced holdings from approved valuations and administrator estimates

evidence.note: RG 94 describes estimates and soft pricing for assets valued infrequently and checking them against hard prices; time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Compare the pool return with its benchmark and the prior day
steps.description: The analyst calculates the day's change in unit value and compares it with the pool benchmark index return and with the change in the prior day's NAV, after allowing for currency moves and cash flows. A difference above the analytical tolerance needs a written explanation such as external manager positioning, fair value timing or a large flow.

error.defect_description: A plausible-looking but wrong explanation is accepted.

control.basis: Unit pricing procedure: analytical review of unit value movement against benchmark (RG 94 tracking of prices against benchmarks)

evidence.note: Tracking against benchmarks and analytical review of NAV movement are described; the 12% unexplained share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Investigate an unexplained movement
steps.description: The analyst asks the custodian to break down the day's NAV change by holding and asks the pool's portfolio manager or external manager liaison about trades and exposures, until the movement is explained or a wrong price, quantity or accrual is found.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: a price is wrong and must be corrected

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Complete the pricing checklist and propose the price
steps.description: The analyst completes the daily pricing checklist with each check's result, attaches the exception explanations and challenge log, and marks the unit value as ready for approval in the shared pricing workbook.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Approval and release with evidence is described; time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Manager reviews and approves the unit price
steps.description: The manager of unit pricing reads the checklist, re-performs the benchmark comparison, looks at every challenged price and override, and either approves the unit value for release or sends it back with questions. The approver must not be the analyst who prepared the checks.

error.defect_description: Approval given without challenging an unusual override.

control.basis: Unit pricing procedure: preparer and approver are different people (internal control over the pools' financial reporting)

evidence.note: Four-eyes approval is standard in fund pricing; times and return rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Re-perform the queried check
steps.description: The analyst answers the manager's questions, re-performs the queried check or obtains the missing evidence, and updates the checklist before resubmitting.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Release the approved price to the custodian and register
steps.description: The analyst confirms the final unit value to the custodian through the portal sign-off so the NAV is finalised, and keys the approved price into the unitholder register for that dealing date so the waiting subscriptions and redemptions can be priced.

error.defect_description: Price keyed into the register with a transposition.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Distribute the price to downstream users
steps.description: The approved price flows to the data warehouse and on to client reporting, performance measurement and investment accounting, and the unit transactions team is notified that the dealing date can be processed. Most prices end here; a few are later found to be wrong.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: price later found to be wrong

evidence.note: A post-release error rate of about 1.5% of pool prices (roughly one or two a month across four pools, mostly small) is an author estimate; no published rate was found.

steps.name: Quantify the price error and affected transactions
steps.description: When fund accounting, the custodian or a later check finds a wrong price, the analyst recalculates the correct unit value for every affected valuation date, measures the error as a percentage of NAV, and lists the subscriptions, redemptions and switches priced at the wrong value with the gain or loss to each client.

error.defect_description: Impact calculation misses a transaction priced at the wrong value.

evidence.note: Sources describe how pricing errors flow through every later transaction and the need to quantify them; detection delay of one to fourteen days is an author estimate.

steps.name: Assess materiality and log the incident
steps.description: The manager compares the error with the NAV error threshold in the pool's error correction policy, considers qualitative factors such as repeated small errors, decides whether transactions must be reprocessed and clients compensated, and logs the incident for enterprise risk.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Pool NAV error correction policy; industry thresholds of 0.3% (RG 94) to 0.5% of NAV (Central Bank of Ireland CP130, CSSF bond funds)

next.condition: at or above the materiality threshold
below threshold: correct going forward only

evidence.note: Thresholds are stated in the sources; the 30% material share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Approve the correction and client notice
steps.description: The vice president of investment operations reviews the proposed reprocessing and compensation, agrees with the custodian who bears the cost when its error caused the problem, and approves the notice that the client relationship managers send to affected clients.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: NAV error correction policy: senior approval of reprocessing, compensation and client communication

evidence.note: Correction, redress and communication steps are described by both sources; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Reprocess unit transactions and settle compensation
steps.description: The analyst reverses and rebooks the affected unit transactions in the register at the corrected prices, the custodian revises its records, and cash or extra units are moved between client accounts and the pool to make each party whole, with the cash team releasing any transfers.

error.defect_description: A rebooked transaction is keyed wrongly.

evidence.note: Compensation by issuing units or paying cash is described by RG 94; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Close the incident and record root cause
steps.description: The manager records the root cause, the amounts and the fixes in the incident log, adds any new check to the pricing procedure, and reports the incident in the monthly operations risk summary.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Operational incident log reviewed by enterprise risk and internal audit (RG 94 good practice on error tracking)

evidence.note: Procedures to track errors and periodic review of incident logs are described; time is an author estimate.

exceptions.name: Weekend or holiday hold
exceptions.description: Friday and pre-holiday prices are reviewed on the next business day, adding two or three days of elapsed time with no work.

exceptions.name: Incomplete or late NAV pack
exceptions.description: A report or manager sub-account is missing and the custodian re-runs the pack.

exceptions.name: Open reconciliation break on a pool account
exceptions.description: The analyst must agree the NAV impact of an unresolved break before continuing.

exceptions.name: Price challenge and NAV re-run
exceptions.description: Out-of-tolerance, stale or missing prices are researched, overridden and the NAV re-run.

exceptions.name: Unexplained movement against benchmark
exceptions.description: The day's change is investigated with the custodian and portfolio managers; sometimes a price is wrong and the challenge loop repeats.

exceptions.name: Manager sends price back
exceptions.description: The approver queries a check and the analyst re-performs it.

exceptions.name: Material price error after release
exceptions.description: A wrong price above the policy threshold is found days later; transactions are reprocessed and clients compensated.

exceptions.name: Immaterial price error after release
exceptions.description: A small error is corrected going forward and logged without reprocessing.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the 4 p.m. valuation point to manager approval of the unit price
benchmarks.population: Daily-priced institutional pools with custodian-calculated NAV and next-morning manager review

evidence.note: Overnight custodian run plus a morning of checks gives approval around 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. on the next business day (0.75 to 0.9 days); Friday and pre-holiday prices, about a quarter of valuation dates, add two to three days, which lifts the median of all dates to about 0.9 days. No published benchmark found.

benchmarks.population: Regulatory and supervisory thresholds for correcting and compensating NAV errors in Australia (0.3%), Ireland (proposed 0.5% for non-money-market funds) and Luxembourg (0.5% bond and mixed, 1.0% equity funds)

evidence.note: Values stated in the sources; the model manager's own policy is not public.

benchmarks.unit: share of pool prices with at least one price challenged to the custodian

evidence.note: Author estimate for global and emerging market equity pools with thousands of holdings.

benchmarks.unit: share of approved pool prices later found wrong (any size)

evidence.note: Author estimate; no public rate for pension pools was found.

pain_points.description: The whole review is compressed into the morning after the custodian's overnight run; a late or incomplete pack or a re-run after price overrides pushes approval past the time unit transactions need the price.

evidence.note: NAV reruns and late data are named breakpoints; impact on this team is an author judgment.

pain_points.description: Price exception reports flag many movements that turn out to be genuine market moves, so analysts spend time clearing false positives while the real errors are prices that move inside the tolerance band.

evidence.note: RG 94 notes stale and out-of-tolerance prices in data feeds; the false positive burden is an author judgment.

pain_points.description: Pricing waits for the reconciliations team to release positions, so a single open break on a pool account can hold up the price.

evidence.note: Unreconciled positions are a stop-the-line criterion in the source.

pain_points.description: The unitholder register is a custodian module supplemented by controlled spreadsheets, so agreeing units outstanding and keying the approved price are manual.

evidence.note: Organisation file assumption about the register; author judgment.

pain_points.description: A price error found days later is expensive because every subscription, redemption and switch since the error must be recalculated, and pools have a few very large unitholders.

evidence.note: RG 94 explains that errors flow through all later transactions until stopped.

sources.title: RG 94 Unit pricing: Guide to good practice
sources.publisher: Australian Securities and Investments Commission and Australian Prudential Regulation Authority
sources.supports: Monitoring controls in unit pricing such as movements outside agreed tolerances and tracking prices against benchmarks; data feeds with stale prices, zero amounts and out-of-tolerance moves; reconciliations in each pricing cycle; incident and error logs; compensation when an error is 0.3% (30 basis points) or more; price as often as units can be bought or sold; batching of applications on the day a price is struck.

sources.title: CP130 Treatment, Correction and Redress of Errors in Investment Funds
sources.supports: Proposed quantitative materiality threshold for NAV errors of 0.50% of NAV for funds other than money market funds (0.10% for money market funds), qualitative factors, aggregation of small errors over several valuation points, and the steps of identification, correction and redress.

sources.title: Circular CSSF 24/856: Protection of investors in case of an NAV calculation error, an instance of non-compliance with the investment rules and other errors at UCI level
sources.publisher: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (Luxembourg)
sources.supports: NAV error tolerance thresholds of 0.50% of NAV for bond and mixed funds, 1.00% for equity funds and 0.20% for money market funds; significant NAV errors must be corrected and notified; replaces Circular CSSF 02/77, the rule in force during 2019 to 2022.

sources.title: NAV Oversight: Controls, Review Workflow, and Common Breakpoints
sources.supports: Eight-step NAV review workflow (readiness, reconciliation review, pricing and stale price oversight, accrual review, investor allocations, analytical review, approval and release, remediation); stop-the-line criteria such as unreconciled positions, missing pricing approvals and unexplained NAV movement; common breakpoints including stale prices, FX inconsistency and NAV reruns.

sources.title: Pooled Funds (BCI web page)
sources.supports: Peer provincial public-sector manager: clients hold units of pooled funds held in trust; unit price is market value divided by units outstanding; public market pools open daily and private market pools typically annually; expenses recovered through the unit value; custodian for public assets; SOC 1 audit of the manager.

sources.title: Public Equity Pooled Fund Financial Statements, December 2021
sources.supports: Units issued and redeemed at a unit value equal to net assets divided by units outstanding on each valuation date, recorded on a trade date basis; open-ended pools where each client's units issued or redeemed depend on changes to its asset allocation; purchase and redemption limits set by the CIO; pool cash and liquidity monitored daily.

sources.title: RFP 24-01 Master Custody Services: Questions and Answers
sources.supports: A public pool operator with 22 pools requires daily pricing of all investments and daily valuation of participant accounts, receives the custodian's NAV daily, and requires a daily compliance report by 9:00 a.m.

sources.title: Reports on Controls at Service Organizations FAQs
sources.publisher: Chartered Professional Accountants of British Columbia
sources.supports: CSAE 3416 (SOC 1 equivalent) reports on controls at a service organization relevant to user entities' financial reporting; Type 1 covers design at a date and Type 2 covers operating effectiveness over a period; used by user entities and their auditors.

sources.title: Wages: Financial analyst (NOC 11101) in the Toronto region
sources.supports: Toronto hourly wages low 27.97, median 41.60, high 73.57 dollars (reference period 2023-2024); the organisation file uses it as the proxy for operations analysts.

sources.title: Wages: Finance director (NOC 10010) in the Toronto region
sources.supports: Toronto hourly wages low 41.21, median 62.37, high 96.15 dollars (reference period 2023-2024); the organisation file uses it for operations managers.

assumptions: The model manager has not published its pricing arrangements; the workflow follows the organisation file's assumption that the custodian calculates daily NAVs and the model manager's unit pricing team reviews and approves them.

The case starts at the 4 p.m. valuation point and ends at manager approval (or, for the 1.5% of prices later found wrong, at incident closure). The validator's p90 is driven by the weekend and holiday hold.

interfaces.triggered_by shares describe which input usually arrives last and releases the case: the custodian's NAV pack almost always, the reconciliations release on some days, and occasionally a new valuation, reference data fix or pool launch.

Time and branch probabilities are author estimates (tier C) because no published time study of pension pool pricing was found; regulatory thresholds and control descriptions come from Australian, Irish and Luxembourg sources, as no current Canadian rule on NAV error thresholds could be opened.

The data analyst (investment data management) and the vice president of investment operations take part although the organisation file's process map lists only four roles for this process; both roles exist in the organisation file.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file: Job Bank Toronto wages deflated 9% to 2021, plus variable pay, times a 1.35 loading factor.

Staffing: about 1.45 analyst FTE on pricing for four pools, with most of the rest of the three analysts' time on unit transactions; stated FTE (about 1.9) is close to the 2.0 implied by hands-on time and volume, and the team of four is fully used across pricing and transfer agency.
